newsitem.title: UK: Chronology of IRA attacks and major bomb finds.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of IRA attacks and major bomb finds.

text.p: Following is a chronology of attacks carried out by the Irish Republican Army and of police actions since the group called off a 17-month-long ceasefire.
February 9, 1996 - A huge bomb rocks London's Docklands commercial district, killing two and injuring 100. The blast came just minutes after the IRA declared its 17-month ceasefire was over.
February 15 - Bomb left in holdall in telephone box in Charing Cross Road, central London. Defused by police.
February 18 - An explosion ripped apart a bus in central London, killing the IRA guerrilla carrying it and injuring nine other people.
February 19 - Police find bomb-making equipment and explosives in London home of dead IRA bomber.
March 9 - A small bomb exploded near West Brompton underground station in London. No injuries.
April 17 - A small bomb exploded in exclusive part of Earl's Court district in west London. No injuries.
April 24 - Two huge bombs placed under London's Hammersmith bridge but failed to detonate. No one was injured by what police said were biggest devices planted by IRA in mainland Britain.
June 15 - Bomb in a van exploded in a shopping centre in northern English city of Manchester injuring over 200 people.
June 28 - Three mortars fired at British army barracks in Osnabruck, Germany. No injuries but several buildings badly damaged.
July 15 - Police arrest seven people in London and seize components for up to 36 bombs believed intended to target utilities installations in London and south-east England.

Sept 23 - Police arrest six people, one of whom killed in shootout, and seize large quantity of explosives, weapons and bomb-making equipment. Police say raids thwarted "serious, imminent IRA terrorist attack" on British mainland.
